title: Write a budget pick in CP-SAT

blocks.text: A school district (not GridCap) funds building repairs from a yearly budget. Its finance office keeps every cost in millions of dollars with two decimals (`1.15` is $1,150,000), and wants the pick made in CP-SAT, because its other planning models already use it.
Write `pick(values, costs, budget)` in `pick.py`. It returns the indices of the repairs to fund, in increasing order, for this model:
**Parameters.** $`v_i`$, the value of repair $`i`$ (a score, with up to two decimals); $`c_i`$, its cost ($M, two decimals); $`B`$, the budget ($M, two decimals).

CP-SAT accepts whole numbers only in a row, so state the budget row in hundredths of a million, where every cost and the budget are whole. Turn each number into hundredths with care: a value such as `1.15 * 100` is not exactly 115 in floating point. Use `cp_model.CpModel`, `new_bool_var`, `add`, `maximize` and `cp_model.CpSolver`, as lesson 4.1.1 did. About ten lines.

Two facts from the lesson you will need. CP-SAT's objective accepts decimal coefficients, so the values may stay as they are, or be scaled to hundredths like the costs; either gives the same pick. And `solver.solve(model)` returns a status: read the plan only when it is `cp_model.OPTIMAL` or `cp_model.FEASIBLE`. Funding nothing always fits the budget, so this model always has a plan.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

SCALE = 100          # hundredths of a million: every cost and the budget is a whole number of these


def pick(values: list[float], costs: list[float], budget: float) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of the repairs to fund, in increasing order: most value with total cost <= budget."""
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    x = [model.new_bool_var(f"x_{i}") for i in range(len(values))]
    whole = [round(c * SCALE) for c in costs]
    model.add(sum(w * xi for w, xi in zip(whole, x)) <= round(budget * SCALE))
    model.maximize(sum(round(v * SCALE) * xi for v, xi in zip(values, x)))
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.solve(model)
    return [i for i in range(len(x)) if solver.value(x[i])]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(pick([3, 4, 5], [0.5, 0.65, 1.2], 1.15))

cases.says: on whole-number data the pick has the most value any affordable set has
the pick costs no more than the budget and lists indices in increasing order
costs with two decimals are compared at full precision, so three items of 1.40 do not fit a budget of 4.00
items whose costs add up to exactly the budget all fit, although the budget times 100 is not exactly a whole number in floating point
